selected_mathematical_checks: The finite-jet billiard example uses four disjoint bumps away from finitely many sample angles and three homogeneous moment constraints, leaving a nonzero smooth perturbation. Small amplitude preserves h+hdoubleprime>0. Scale and translation normalization are retained, while equality to a circle on an arc rules out an ellipse. This obstructs finite support-jet data, not genuine invariant caustics.

In the source plateau construction all complex differences are included, the fixed finite slope set gives H>0 and gap at least 2H, and a crossed cut has one upward monomial dominating every downward source by h^H. Under measurable a<=k<=b and |R|b h^H<=a/2, the upward cut is at least (a/2)h^m, hence active drift at least aHh^m. Absolute continuity of the finite affine minimum permits the a.e. derivative argument.

The affine gap from x to c is at most 2d/h on B_h, so the displayed time 2d/(a H h^(m+1)) is safe. A compact initial Q gives one starting scale, and capped square roots reach h_P in finitely many steps. The source uses successive box containment, not unproved nesting of plateaux. These are positive-box-rate consequences, not PE permanence.

For the simple strongly connected monomolecular graph, L=(n-1)K makes Q+LI entrywise nonnegative. The chosen simple path has length at most n-1. Restrict its time-ordered Peano term to consecutive disjoint T-windows, so its integral is a product of edge integrals >=alpha^m. Retaining the global e^-LH factor gives beta for every matrix entry, including the zero-length diagonal path. The bound holds on each rolling H window.

Column stochasticity gives n beta<=1; subtracting b 11^T with b=beta/2 leaves theta times a column-stochastic matrix, theta=1-nb in [1/2,1). On equal-mass differences the rank-one term vanishes. Products yield theta^floor((t-s)/H), while the residual interval is l1 nonexpansive. This is common-forcing synchronization, not equilibrium convergence.

In A+B reversible with 2B the physical ratio r=A/B satisfies exactly rprime=-Ma r+Mb. Each length-v interval contains floor(v/T) full windows. Backward T-block summation gives R=MKT/(1-exp(-M alpha)); the final window gives ell=M alpha exp(-MKT). The chosen N makes the transient ratio term <=1, yielding B>=M/(2+R) and A>=M ell/(1+ell). The compact mass-range constants are safe monotone bounds.
The same nonlinear model has Bprime<=MK B, so no common entrance time can hold over all positive initial data approaching B=0. This does not refute compact-initial uniformity.

The 2A reversible with 3A periodic schedule has both integrals exactly one on every length-two window. Its initial pure-forward phase starting at x=2 solves xprime=x² and blows up at 1/2 before the reverse phase. This refutes only the unbounded-class PE extension.

A common compact positive set invariant under every fresh PE schedule would be invariant under the initial pure A-to-B time-one map. Iterating that one map within the same set forces A to zero. The iterated all-forward schedule need not be PE: the contradiction is to the universal set-invariance property, not to eventual PE bounds.

On a bounded class, consumption terms contain the consumed coordinate, so bounded coefficients give x_i prime>=-C x_i and prevent finite-time boundary hitting. That one-sided estimate alone does not prove uniform eventual boundary repulsion for arbitrary networks. Integrated bare rates cannot simply replace integrated state-weighted fluxes.
